summary.exchange_note: One exchange per taxonomy.md §0.8 rule 11. Reviewer conceded severity on the three en items (minor -> major). Author and reviewer still disagree on the two gold zh 的-for-得 items, so they are escalated to the developer and not discarded, because they are user-adjudicated gold rows.

gold_readme_finding: Partly confirmed, but the author's conclusion does not follow from it. tests/fixtures/dt_gold/README.md (Provenance, 'Clean items') does describe clean items as differing 'only by acceptable variation (synonym, contraction, kana/kanji or 得/的 variant, optional comma)'. However, none of the 10 zh clean items contains a 得/的 difference (the diffs are 8 synonyms, 1 exact copy and 1 dropped comma). Meanwhile zh_seed_11 (note 'de-particle 得→的: 画得→画的') and zh_multi_02 both carry 画的很细致 -> 画得很细致 as de_particles/minor, and the README's adjudication table records ZH as 'Approved as presented' by the developer. So the README prose and the adjudicated data disagree. The item-level labels are the developer's signed-off ruling; the README line is generic boilerplate. It probably means 的/地, or it was never instantiated. Fix the README line either way once the escalation is decided.

items.author_position: 的-for-得 is contested in taxonomy.md (C11 bars it as a positive), and the DT gold README lists '得/的 variant' as acceptable, so the item becomes clean.
items.reviewer_position: v6 de_particle exempts only 的-for-地. taxonomy.md calls 的-for-得 'wrong in 规范 text', and the DT reference is 规范 text. C11 bars contested forms as positives AND as hard negatives, so it cannot justify variant_ok either. The developer adjudicated this exact item as a minor error.
items.exchange: Author's strongest argument (the README clean-item convention) does not change the reviewer's mind: no clean item instantiates it, and the item-level adjudication outranks README boilerplate.
